{{Quote|Get a shuttle ready. I shall assume full responsibility to losing them and apologize to Lord Vader.|Captain Lorth Needa|audio=ThisIsABadIdea-ESB.flac|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
The '''TIE/sh VIP shuttle''' was a short-range [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] manufactured by [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]]. The personnel priority model was one of the more successful variants of the basic [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]], affording room for up to four individuals as well as additional cargo. Although the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] was sluggish and not designed for combat, it was equipped with a [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] and a [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] and was typically used by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to quickly ferry [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers]] between [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and other installations. The TIE/sh was an unpopular mode of [[Transport/Legends|transportation]] among users, as they preferred the luxury of the larger [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class shuttle]].

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] [[Pilot/Legends|flew]] a TIE/sh to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Jerne]] in pursuit of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], but the pair evaded Vader and fled using his shuttle. The [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] made extensive use of the TIE/sh in the subsequent [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Hoth campaign]] of [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], employing the shuttle as a substitute for standard [[Comm unit/Legends|comm]] traffic between Vader's [[Death Squadron/Legends|squadron]] of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], which would have interfered with the mission's vital [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] scans and [[Viper probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] transmissions in the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]]. [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]] of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']] made his final [[Realspace/Legends|space]] voyage aboard a TIE/sh before his [[Death/Legends|execution]] at Vader's hands for failing to capture the Rebel [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|starship]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. Several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] following the Empire's defeat at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Imperial leaders such as [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kentor Sarne]] and [[Supreme Warlord]] [[Blitzer Harrsk]] rode the TIE shuttle as their personal transports.

Long after, in [[44 ABY]], the world [[Nam Chorios/Legends|Nam Chorios']] [[Mayor/Legends|Mayor]] [[Snaplaunce]] had repurposed his TIE/sh as a personal [[Politics/Legends|campaign]] vehicle, appropriately named ''[[Vote Snaplaunce]]''. [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Luke and [[Ben Skywalker]] and their [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] ally, [[Vestara Khai]], borrowed the shuttle in their hunt for the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] entity [[Abeloth]], and, despite the craft's age and limited maneuverability, they took advantage of the equipment in its dual pods to survive an attack by Abeloth's [[Ship (Sith Meditation Sphere)|ship]]. While the TIE/sh was heavily damaged, the group converted it into a wind-propelled [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] to resume their travels.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|So we have a few control chips, plenty of serviceable wire, power output meters, emergency start-up capacitators&hellip;''"<br />"''Stang!|Vestara Khai and Ben Skywalker, examining their damaged TIE shuttle's cannon support systems|audio=VestaraKhai-TIEshuttle.flac|<ref name="Conviction" />}}
The [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]]&ndash;manufactured<ref name="Databank" /> TIE/sh VIP shuttle,<ref name="Age of Rebellion" /> otherwise known as the TIE shuttle,<ref name="Databank" /> was a variant model of the basic [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]]. Similar to the [[TIE/br boarding shuttle]], the TIE/sh adopted the TIE [[Bomber/Legends|bomber's]] [[Hull/Legends|hull]] configuration but replaced the bomber's portside ordnance launcher and the [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]] delivery system with a small, well-appointed passenger pod. The pod could hold up to four individuals<ref name="Age of Rebellion" /> and additional cargo,<ref name="RECG" /> containing two rows of front-facing seats<ref name="AJ10" /> that had space for two [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and were equipped with [[Restraint harness|straps]]. Each TIE [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] wing had an array of three [[Solar collector/Legends|solar panels]],<ref name="Conviction" /> and the [[Starship/Legends|craft]] either had its wings bent inward, similar to the TIE bomber,<ref name="Databank" /> or bent outward.<ref name="ESB" /> A [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] controlled the craft and simultaneously served as the [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]]<ref name="GG3" /> using [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]]-style controls from the starboard [[Cockpit/Legends|command pod]].<ref name="Conviction" />

[[File:TIEShuttle-AJ10.png|thumb|left|260px|TIE/sh VIP shuttle schematics]]
The TIE/sh measured 7.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length and, while not designed for combat,<ref name="Databank" /> protected its passengers<ref name="AJ10" /> with a single,<ref name="RECG" /> lower-powered<ref name="Starships & Vehicles">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|70|Starship & Vehicle Directory}}</ref> [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] with relevant support systems<ref name="Conviction" /> that could be set to autofire mode<ref name="RECG" /> and that had an [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheric]] firing range of 2.5 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]],<ref name="GG3" /> though the shuttle required a starfighter escort if danger was nearby.<ref name="Starships & Vehicles" /> Designed for short-range [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel,<ref name="BTM" /> sluggish, and difficult to maneuver,<ref name="Conviction" /> the TIE/sh generally lacked a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and other advances<ref name="BTM" /> but nonetheless mounted a defensive [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]]<ref name="Age of Rebellion" /> and was equipped with [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]].<ref name="GG3" />

The cockpit was illuminated by lights and had a control board that included a main [[Computer monitor/Legends|monitor screen]], which provided diagnostic warnings via flashing [[Color/Legends|yellow]] and red alerts, and a sensor screen. Another sensor board was located in the passenger pod, from which the sensors could be recalibrated and read to assist the pilot's flying. Communication between the pods was facilitated by an internal [[Intercom/Legends|intercom]], while a [[Comm unit/Legends|comm system]] automatically connected to a [[TIE pilot]] [[Helmet/Legends|helmet's]] voice-activated [[Microphone/Legends|microphone]] and manually accessible by both pods could be used for external contact.<ref name="Conviction" /> The shuttle boasted a cargo capacity of up to one [[Metric ton/Legends|metric ton]]<ref name="Databank" /> and two [[Standard day/Legends|days']] worth of consumables.<ref name="RECG" />

Customary of the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE series]], the TIE/sh sported [[Twin ion engine/Legends|twin ion engines]],<ref name="AJ10" /> which were capable of achieving a maximum atmospheric speed of 650 [[Kilometer per hour/Legends|km/h]],<ref name="Age of Rebellion" /> as well as [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]] for take-off and landing.<ref name="Conviction" /> Both the TIE/sh and the TIE/br were equipped with landing gear, which, for a [[Time/Legends|time]], made them the only TIE series craft not dependent upon the docking racks found aboard larger [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] ships and bases.<ref name="Starships & Vehicles" /> A [[Entry ramp/Legends|boarding ramp]] extended from the undersides of both the shuttle's cockpit<ref name="Dark Knight's Devilry">{{StoryCite|story=Dark Knight's Devilry|book=The Empire Strikes Back Monthly 153}}</ref> and passenger pod,<ref name="RECG" /> but each of the pods also had its own top hatch.<ref name="Conviction" /> Available only to the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]],<ref name="RECG" /> the TIE/sh was not available for public sale.<ref name="GG3" /> The craft marketed at 120,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] new and 45,000 credits used.<ref name="RECG" /> The shuttle also had emergency tools that included an [[Arc welder/Legends|arc welder]].<ref name="Conviction" />

==Role==
{{Quote|A kind of ship's boat used to ferry small numbers of personnel between naval ships and ground stations.|Bakki Sourthol, writing on TIE shuttles in an Alliance report on the TIE Series|<ref name="AJ10" />}}
The Galactic Empire utilized the TIE/sh as a specialized priority shuttle for quickly [[Transport/Legends|transporting]]<ref name="AJ10" /> command-level [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers]],<ref name="Databank" /> [[Trooper/Legends|troops]],<ref name="BTM" /> and other priority cargo between [[Imperial Navy/Legends|naval]] ships,<ref name="AJ10" /> such as [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]],<ref name="BTM" /> as well as [[Space station/Legends|space stations]]<ref name="RECG" /> and ground installations.<ref name="AJ10" /> Efficient but utilitarian, the TIE/sh was an unpopular mode of transportation for those who used the craft, as they coveted the more luxurious [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]].<ref name="Starships & Vehicles" /> Indeed, while [[Flag officer/Legends|flag officers]] typically used the larger ''Lambda''-class shuttle, lower-ranking [[Officer/Legends|officers]] usually rode aboard the TIE/sh.<ref name="Databank" /> Each Imperial ship in a [[line]] carrying [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] typically also carried one TIE/sh.<ref name="AJ10" />

==History==
===Height of the Empire===
{{Quote|One variant of the TIE bomber replaces the warhead bay with a cargo bay for passengers.|Admiral Motti, ''Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''|<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>}}
TIE/sh VIP shuttle was one of several mission-specific TIE Series models that Sienar Fleet Systems developed for the Galactic Empire,<ref name="AJ10" /> and alongside the TIE/br boarding shuttle was among the most successful variants of the TIE bomber.<ref name="Starships & Vehicles" /> [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] provided a brief mention of the passenger variant as [[Author/Legends|author]] of the Imperial Navy chapter of the ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'' tactical manual, distributed just prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]<ref name="Handbook" /> [[0 BBY/Legends|nineteen years]] into the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Empire's reign]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

[[File:ByeByeJerne-DKD.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Luke Skywalker and Leia Organa flee Jerne using Darth Vader's TIE shuttle.]]
Between [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Date-DKD">''[[Dark Knight's Devilry]]'' takes place following the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction of Alderaan]] and the events of {{Film|IV}} while [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] still uses [[Anakin Skywalker's second lightsaber/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's lightsaber]], which he [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|loses]] during the events of {{Film|V}}. This [[Time/Legends|time]] period corresponds to the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> while in pursuit of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] piloted a TIE/sh over the [[Desert/Legends|sandy wastes]] of the ancient [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Jerne]] with Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Ryko Vant]] aboard. Vader had lured the Rebels to the Imperial outpost [[Adony Station]], where he planned to [[Mission to Jerne|capture]] them while they searched for the purported [[Eternity Crystal]]&mdash;the Rebels had hoped that it would allow them to [[Time travel/Legends|turn back time]] and prevent the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan's]] [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]]. However, Skywalker and Organa eluded Vader's trap at Adony Station and escaped Jerne aboard the TIE/sh.<ref name="Dark Knight's Devilry" />

In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]],<ref name="Date-SWAJ">{{JournalCite|10|Alliance Intelligence Report: TIE Fighters}} is intended as a tie-in to the sourcebook ''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]'', which is set in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]].</ref> Rebel Alliance [[Lieutenant Commander/Legends|Lieutenant Commander]] [[Bakki Sourthol]] filed a report on the Empire's TIE Series starfighters for the [[Task Force on Alliance Security]]. The compiled report, which detailed the development of the TIE Series and its many variant models, contained detailed TIE/sh technical specifications, including a set of schematics.<ref name="AJ10" />

[[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader's personal [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], extensively utilized the TIE/sh while searching for the Rebel Alliance during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Hoth campaign]]<ref name="GG3" /> in 3 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]].<ref name="NEC" /> Because standard comm traffic between the fleet's Star Destroyers would have interfered with vital sensor scans and communications from dispatched [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]], Death Squadron employed TIE shuttles rather than the high-profile ''Lambda''-class shuttle to physically deliver non-vital messages back and forth when the fleet was not in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:TIEShuttle-ESBHD.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Captain Needa's TIE/sh departs the Imperial Star Destroyer ''Avenger'' during the Hoth campaign.]]
Captain [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]] of the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']]<ref name="GG3" /> made his final space voyage in a TIE/sh in the wake of the Battle of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="BTM" /> After the ''Avenger'' lost the Rebel agent [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and his fugitive [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|freighter]], the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], while pursuing it through the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]], Needa instructed his [[M'Kae/Legends|communications officer]] to prepare a TIE/sh;<ref name="ESB" /> the captain rode it<ref name="BTM" /> from the ''Avenger'' to Vader's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], to personally apologize to the Dark Lord for allowing the Rebel [[YT-series/Legends|ship]] to escape. Vader summarily [[Death/Legends|executed]] Needa for his failure.<ref name="ESB" />

===Fall of Imperial leadership===
{{RPG|"[[Endgame (adventure)|Endgame]]"}}
{{Quote|Captain Brannij, send over your shuttle; mine has been damaged in all the scuffle.|Moff Sarne, requesting a TIE shuttle to evacuate him from battle|<ref name="Endgame">{{DarkStryder|adventure=Endgame (adventure)|book=Endgame}}</ref>}}
[[8 ABY/Legends|Four years after]] the Empire's defeat<ref name="Endgame" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]<ref name="NEC" /> at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kentor Sarne]] attempted to flee the [[Battle of Kathol System]] via a TIE shuttle. [[Moff Sarne's forces]] had been losing the battle to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] crew of the ''[[FarStar]]'' [[CR90 corvette/Legends|corvette]] and Sarne had personally made a last-ditch attempt to [[Weapon/Legends|weaponize]] a [[launch gate]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of the planet [[Kathol (planet)|Kathol]]. While the ''FarStar'' crew damaged the moff's ''Lambda''-class shuttle aboard the launch gate, Sarne requested Captain [[Brannij]] of his Star Destroyer, [[Bastion (Imperial II-class)|''Bastion'']], to deploy a TIE shuttle that would return him to the ''Bastion'' and subsequently leave the [[Kathol system/Legends|Kathol system]] via hyperspace. However, the ''FarStar'' crew was able to avert the gate's activation<ref name="Endgame" /> and kill Sarne before he could escape with the ''Bastion''.<ref name="Warlords1">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-1|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

[[File:ImperialStarfighters-RECG.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A docked TIE/sh (left), among other Imperial starfighters]]
[[12 ABY/Legends|Eight years after]] the [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] battle, [[Supreme Warlord]] [[Blitzer Harrsk]], formerly one of the most respected minds in the Imperial Military, met his demise at the controls of a TIE/sh. Harrsk had previously suffered a traumatic [[Brain/Legends|brain]] injury during the Battle of Endor, causing him to adopt an insane [[Multiple personality disorder|dual persona]] as Captain [[Bolla Thoath]], his former [[Executive officer/Legends|second-in-command]], who had died at Endor. Returning from a [[Imperial Reunification|meeting]] with Admiral [[Natasi Daala]] and other Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] at the [[Tsoss Beacon/Legends|Tsoss Beacon]] [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]]&mdash;in which Daala murdered all present, with the exception of Harrsk, whose brain injury had saved him from Daala's [[Nerve toxin/Legends|poison gas]]&mdash;Harrsk's Thoath persona, determined to end Harrsk's madness, abruptly threw their shuttle into a tailspin. As the two personalities struggled for control of the craft, Harrsk came to the sudden, shattering realization of his own insanity and suicidally slammed the TIE/sh into the asteroid, killing them both.<ref name="Warlords2">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-2|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref>

===''Vote Snaplaunce''===
{{Quote|You have a TIE shuttle.''"<br />"''Indeed.''"<br />"''I'm not sure I can recall ever seeing one in private hands.|Luke Skywalker and Snaplaunce|audio=VoteSnaplaunce.flac|<ref name="Conviction" />}}
In the [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] following the collapse of the Empire, a retired [[Unidentified Imperial mechanic|mechanic]] formerly of the Imperial Navy settled on the planet [[Nam Chorios/Legends|Nam Chorios]]<ref name="Conviction" /> around [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]],<ref name="Date-FOTJ">In ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'', [[Snaplaunce]] remarks that he purchased his [[Vote Snaplaunce|TIE shuttle]] from a retired [[Unidentified Imperial mechanic|Imperial mechanic]] who settled on [[Nam Chorios/Legends|Nam Chorios]] "about fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] ago." ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''Fate of the Jedi: Conviction'' to [[44 ABY]], thereby placing the [[Technician/Legends|mechanic's]] arrival on Nam Chorios around [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]].</ref> where he carefully restored and sold Imperial vessels to private owners. Among the vehicles the [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]] sold was a disarmed TIE/sh to an [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] named [[Snaplaunce]], who proceeded to paint the ship a bright yellow and adorn its external hull with his [[Politics/Legends|campaign]] slogan for the [[Mayor/Legends|mayoral]] office of [[Hweg Shul]], [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of Nam Chorios: "Vote Snaplaunce," which was also registered as the shuttle's official name. The Ithorian modified ''[[Vote Snaplaunce]]'' for civilian use so that the shuttle effectively served as both his personal transport and a traveling campaign advertisement.<ref name="Conviction" />

[[File:SithMeditationSphere2-FF98.png|thumb|left|230px|Luke Skywalker, Ben Skywalker, and Vestara Khai's TIE shuttle was attacked by Ship, a Sith Meditation Sphere (pictured).]]
''Vote Snaplaunce'' remained in the mayor's personal service by<ref name="Conviction" /> [[44 ABY]],<ref name="Date-FOTJ" /> when [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] Luke Skywalker of the [[New Jedi Order]], accompanied by his son, [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Ben Skywalker]], and [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] member [[Vestara Khai]], arrived on Nam Chorios in pursuit of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] entity known as [[Abeloth]]. Snaplaunce, a previous acquaintance of Skywalker's, agreed to loan his shuttle to the motley group of Humans to aid in their quest.<ref name="Conviction" />

With the elder Skywalker at the controls, ''Vote Snaplaunce'' soon fell under attack by [[Ship (Sith Meditation Sphere)|Ship]], a [[Sith Meditation Sphere]] in the service of Abeloth, and [[Koval Station]] from orbit. Although Skywalker's monitors were knocked out of commission, he worked in tandem with his passengers via intercom to evade the attacks and flee the skirmish. Due to battle damage and complications brought about by [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotage]], the TIE shuttle spun out of control in the atmosphere for a time and its [[Engine/Legends|engines]] gave out, but Skywalker was nevertheless able to maneuver it safely onto the ground. In the absence of engine thrust, and with timely repairs on the TIE/sh rendered impractical under the circumstances, the group took advantage of ''Vote Snaplaunce''{{'s}} repulsorlifts and physically pushed the ship to a more sheltered spot before effecting repairs.<ref name="Conviction" />

The group resorted to rigging a sail rudder on top of the shuttle, operating its arc welder with the ship's power to fit the rudder in the span between the twin pods. They also attached wires and cables to the solar panels' trailing edges that connected to the wheels of each pod's top hatch, serving as a pulley. Deeming their work a "[[Bantha fodder/Legends|bantha poodoo]]" [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]], the group proceeded to continue pursuing Abeloth, frantically steering their rigged craft through a hilly route as they were propelled by the port ion engine, reaching nearly fifty km/h.<ref name="Conviction" />

Skywalker's team eventually abandoned the TIE/sh outside Hweg Shul, though [[Media/Legends|media]] interests reported that ''Vote Snaplaunce'' was later recovered. The [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] subsequently jested to [[Holojournalist/Legends|journalists]] [[Kandra Nilitz]] and [[Beurth Ogh]] if they would like to know of Abeloth and the Lost Tribe of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] or receive a complicated account of how his group managed to operate the shuttle; Nilitz took the former offer. During a subsequent [[Operation Shieldfall|battle]] against Abeloth and the Sith Tribe, Khai rigged a [[Capacitor/Legends|capacitor]] from the shuttle to explode a small [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[tsil]] [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]], causing a [[death convulsion]] that incapacitated her and the Skywalkers' opponents to allow their own escape.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Concept to creation===
{{Quote|The fleet around Vader's Star Destroyer now includes Needa's Star Destroyer, the ''Avenger''. Needa's shuttle departs for Vader's Star Destroyer.|''The Empire Strikes Back''{{'s}} screenplay|<ref name="Screenplays">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Tieboardingcraft.jpg|thumb|right|315px|Unused TIE boarding craft concept art for ''A New Hope'', a design resurrected as the TIE shuttle for ''The Empire Strikes Back'', where the wings bend outward instead]]
The shuttle was first mentioned in [[Donald F. Glut]]'s<ref name="ESBn">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> [[April]] [[1980]] [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] of the [[original trilogy]] film that was released in the [[May|following month]]<ref name="YearByYear">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref>&mdash;[[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]&mdash;in which it first appeared.<ref name="ESB" /> The TIE shuttle's design, which is basically a TIE bomber without the bomb chute, dates back to the original concept stages of<ref name="Databank" /> the first ''[[Star Wars]]'' film, [[1977]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']],<ref name="Screenplays" /> in which a twin-pod boarding vehicle was to be seen among the Imperial forces. The idea was dropped from Episode IV before being resurrected for ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="Databank" />

The TIE shuttle in storyboard sketches and the model itself that appears in the film had wings that bent outward, unlike other TIE vessels. However, later depictions of the shuttle show it with wings bent inward, including the image provided in the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]],<ref name="Databank" /> which is an image of a TIE bomber with its bomb chute edited out.<ref name="Anil-Pablo">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/1147959506782973952|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=07-07-2019|quote=I don't believe the model has ever been found, but the storyboard art has the bent-outward wings. The photography of the TIE bomber-style shuttle is literally the TIE bomber model with the bomb chute Photoshopped out.|archivedate=20190722121835|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: "Do you know if the model used for Captain Needa's TIE shuttle in The Empire Strikes Back has outward curved wings? [&hellip;] it looks similar to the TIE bomber in older sources."}}</ref>

===Naming and specifications===
[[File:TIEshuttle-GG3.png|thumb|left|250px|The TIE/sh VIP shuttle, as depicted in ''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']]
The craft that appears in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' was first provided its formal classification as a "TIE/sh" in the article "[[Alliance Intelligence Report: TIE Fighters]]," written by [[Timothy S. O'Brien]] for the May [[1996]] [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 10|tenth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'', a supplement to the [[West End Games]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. Written from an [[in-universe]] perspective by Rebel Alliance starfighter pilot Bakki Sourthol, the article designates the ship as a TIE shuttle and also provides its technical specifications,<ref name="AJ10" /> which are reused for the publisher's [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back''{{'s}} second edition]], released in [[July]] that year.<ref name="GG3" /> The [[1998]] CD-ROM ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' by [[LucasArts]] alternatively identifies the craft as a "Transport Shuttle."<ref name="BTM" />

With the advent of [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' [[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion (roleplaying game)|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'']] [[Star Wars Roleplaying|roleplaying game]], the TIE/sh received a new set of technical specifications that differs from its original West End Games stats, as well as a new designation, the TIE/sh VIP shuttle. The July [[2014]] [[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]] changed the TIE/sh's atmospheric speed from 1,050 km/h to 650 km/h, upgraded its maximum number of passengers from two to four, and specified that it was equipped with a [[Deflector shield/Legends|shield]] generator.<ref name="Age of Rebellion" /><ref name="GG3" /> The [[2011]] novel ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Conviction]]'' by [[Aaron Allston]] had firmly established that the TIE shuttle had only two seats for the Human characters Ben Skywalker and Vestara Khai as a part of the plot,<ref name="Conviction" /> but given that this fact does not necessarily contradict ''Age of Rebellion''{{'s}} specification that the craft could hold up to four individuals, the article assumes that both sources are correct.<ref name="Age of Rebellion" />

The [[Imperial Veterans Expansion Pack|''Imperial Veterans'' Expansion Pack]] supplement to Fantasy Flight Games' ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Miniatures Game]]'' also restricts the passenger number to two individuals if the player upgrades their TIE bomber into a TIE shuttle.<ref name="IVEP">{{FFGXW|set=Imperial Veterans Expansion Pack|cardname=TIE Shuttle}}</ref>

===Canonical ambiguity===
The [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] story "[[Dark Knight's Devilry]]," published by [[Marvel Comics]] in the [[The Empire Strikes Back Monthly 153|153rd issue]] of ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Monthly]]'' with writing by [[Steve Moore]] and illustrations by [[Alan Davis]]<ref name="Dark Knight's Devilry" /> in [[January]] [[1982]],<ref name="Epic">''[[Star Wars Legends Epic Collection: The Original Marvel Years Vol. 3]]''</ref> features Darth Vader piloting a "[[Scout ship/Legends|scout ship]]"<ref name="Dark Knight's Devilry" /> that appears identical to the TIE shuttle;<ref name="Databank" /> however, as both the TIE/sh and the TIE/br boarding shuttle are virtually indistinguishable visually,<ref name="Databank" /><ref name="ICS">''[[Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> certain ambiguity arises as to the [[Scout/Legends|scout]] ship's classification. Yet given that the scout ship's port-side passenger pod displays an ovular inset,<ref name="Dark Knight's Devilry" /> different from the more circular inset of the TIE/br, as illustrated in the 1998 reference book ''[[Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections]]'',<ref name="ICS" /> this article treats the ''Dark Knight's Devilry'' craft as a TIE/sh.

[[File:Battleofkathol.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The battle in "Endgame" from which Moff Sarne attempts to flee via his TIE shuttle]]
The 1996 "[[Endgame (adventure)|Endgame]]" adventure in the ''[[Endgame]]'' supplement to ''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game''{{'s}} ''[[The DarkStryder Campaign]]'' gives several suggestions for the players' final chapter with Moff Sarne, who is attempting to activate the launch gate and flee aboard a TIE shuttle, spelled as "TIE/shuttle," back to the Star Destroyer ''Bastion''. Players, who roleplay as the crew of the ''FarStar'', could kill Sarne before he flees and then work to prevent the launch gate from activating or stop the gate's activation first, in the process letting him escape on his shuttle; if the players are successful either way, the [[Roleplaying game|game]] ends with them defeating Moff Sarne's plans and preventing the gate's activation.<ref name="Endgame" />

The "last resort" option that the game suggests involves a frustrated Captain Brannij helping the ''FarStar'' crew by instructing its members how to deactivate the launch gate and also blowing up Sarne's TIE shuttle before surrendering the remaining Imperial forces to the New Republic.<ref name="Endgame" /> The first part of the "[[The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire]]" article, published on StarWars.com on [[December 5]], [[2013]], confirms that the moff was killed by a crew member of the ''FarStar''&mdash;[[Jessa Dajus]]&mdash;before he could escape with the ''Bastion''.<ref name="Warlords1" />
